\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بحران} (bohrân)}{بحران (bohrân)}]{\fa{بحران} (bohrân) — a crisis}

\label{lesson:FA-C377-bohran}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to happen, then the Persian for to admit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بحران}}
\textbf{\fa{بحران}} (\emph{bohrân}) — \textquotedblleft{}a crisis\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کشور} \fa{در} \fa{یک} \fa{بحران} \fa{بزرگ} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{keshvar dar yek bohrân-e bozorg ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The country is in a big crisis.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{bohrânhâ}. \emph{Bohrâni} — critical.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{بحران}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{buḥrān} \textquotedblleft{}crisis\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); Persian also forms the adjective \emph{bohrâni} \textquotedblleft{}critical\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bohrân}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bohrân}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to happen, then the Persian for to admit, then say \emph{bohrân} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{راه} \fa{حل} (râh-e hall)}{راه حل (râh-e hall)}]{\fa{راه} \fa{حل} (râh-e hall) — a solution}

\label{lesson:FA-C377-rah-e-hall}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to admit, then the Persian for a crisis.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{راه} \fa{حل}}
\textbf{\fa{راه} \fa{حل}} (\emph{râh-e hall}) — \textquotedblleft{}a solution\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برای} \fa{این} \fa{مشکل} \fa{یک} \fa{راه} \fa{حل} \fa{ساده} \fa{پیدا} \fa{کردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{barâye in moshkel yek râh-e hall-e sâde peydâ kardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We found a simple solution to this problem.
\end{quote}

\emph{Râh} \textquotedblleft{}way\textquotedblright{} + ezafe + \emph{hall} \textquotedblleft{}solving\textquotedblright{}. Plural \emph{râh-e hallhâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{راه} \fa{حل}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}the way of solving\textquotedblright{}: \emph{râh} \textquotedblleft{}road, way\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian (EtymDB traces it back through Proto-Iranian), and \emph{hall} \textquotedblleft{}solving\textquotedblright{} comes from Arabic \emph{ḥall}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{râh-e hall}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{râh-e hall}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{râh-e hall}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to admit, then the Persian for a crisis, then say \emph{râh-e hall} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{راه} \fa{حل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A solution\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جلوگیری} \fa{کردن} (jolowgiri kardan)}{جلوگیری کردن (jolowgiri kardan)}]{\fa{جلوگیری} \fa{کردن} (jolowgiri kardan) — to prevent}

\label{lesson:FA-C377-jelogiri-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a crisis, then the Persian for a solution.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جلوگیری} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{جلوگیری} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{jolowgiri kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to prevent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پلیس} \fa{از} \fa{تصادف} \fa{جلوگیری} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{polis az tasâdof jolowgiri kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police prevented an accident.
\end{quote}

Takes \emph{az}: \emph{az chizi jolowgiri kardan}. \emph{Jolow} \textquotedblleft{}front\textquotedblright{} + \emph{giri} \textquotedblleft{}taking\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{جلوگیری} \fa{کردن}} is native Persian, built from \emph{jolow} \textquotedblleft{}front\textquotedblright{} + \emph{giri} \textquotedblleft{}taking\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{gir-}, the present stem of \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{}, + \emph{kardan}. To prevent is to take the front, to block the way.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jolowgiri kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jolowgiri kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{jolowgiri kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a crisis, then the Persian for a solution, then say \emph{jolowgiri kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{جلوگیری} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To prevent\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پیشگیری} (pishgiri)}{پیشگیری (pishgiri)}]{\fa{پیشگیری} (pishgiri) — prevention}

\label{lesson:FA-C377-pishgiri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a solution, then the Persian for to prevent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پیشگیری}}
\textbf{\fa{پیشگیری}} (\emph{pishgiri}) — \textquotedblleft{}prevention\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پیشگیری} \fa{بهتر} \fa{از} \fa{درمان} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pishgiri behtar az darmân ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Prevention is better than cure.
\end{quote}

\emph{Pish} \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{} + \emph{giri} \textquotedblleft{}taking\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Pishgiri kardan} — to prevent (an illness).

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{پیشگیری}} is a native Persian compound built from \emph{pish} \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{} + \emph{giri} \textquotedblleft{}taking\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{gir-}, the present stem of \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{}: taking hold of a problem before it comes.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اهمیت} \fa{داشتن} (ahamiyat dâshtan)}{اهمیت داشتن (ahamiyat dâshtan)}]{\fa{اهمیت} \fa{داشتن} (ahamiyat dâshtan) — to matter, to be important}

\label{lesson:FA-C377-ahamiyyat-dashtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to prevent, then the Persian for prevention.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اهمیت} \fa{داشتن}}
\textbf{\fa{اهمیت} \fa{داشتن}} (\emph{ahamiyat dâshtan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to matter, to be important\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برای} \fa{من} \fa{نظر} \fa{تو} \fa{اهمیت} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{barâye man nazar-e to ahamiyat dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Your opinion matters to me.
\end{quote}

\emph{Ahamiyyat} \textquotedblleft{}importance\textquotedblright{} + \emph{dâshtan}. \emph{Ahamiyyat nadârad} — it doesn't matter.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{اهمیت}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ahammiyya} \textquotedblleft{}importance\textquotedblright{}, from the same Arabic family as \emph{mohem} \textquotedblleft{}important\textquotedblright{}; \emph{dâshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to have\textquotedblright{} is the inherited Persian verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
